shortDescription: Manage object and system privileges in Oracle database

options.name: convert_to_upper
options.description: Converts all entries for role and objs parameters silently to upper case to simulate case insensitivity

options.name: dsn
options.description: Oracle Data Source Name (connect string or TNS alias), overrides hostname/port/service_name

options.name: mode
options.description: The mode with which to connect to the database

options.name: objs
options.description: When setting object privileges, list the objects the privileges are set for. Use format SCHEMA_NAME.OBJECT_NAME Wildcard (%) can be used in OBJECT_NAME part, for example HR.% to set privileges for all objects (with type objecttype) in schema HR. Object names are CASE SENSITIVE, so by default use UPPER CASE.

options.name: objtypes
options.description: When using object privileges, list also the object types (from OBJECT_TYPE column from DBA_OBJECTS).

options.name: port
options.description: The listener port number on the host

options.name: privs
options.description: Privileges to grant or revoke Can be either system privileges (then objs parameter must not be specified) or object privileges (objs parameter must also be set)

options.name: quiet
options.description: If set to False, all executed commands are returned as Ansible output message

options.name: roles
options.description: List of user names and role names to set permissions to. Names are CASE SENSITIVE So by default use UPPER CASE.

options.name: service_name
options.description: The database service name to connect to

options.name: state
options.description: If present, then privileges are granted, if absent then privileges are revoked

options.name: user
options.description: The Oracle user name to connect to the database, must have DBA privilege
